memory_update.text: HMDPF / TSX:HPS.A is the cleanest direct public mapping found for dry-type transformers, cast-resin transformers, power-quality products, reactors, and engineered magnetics; primary listing is Canada, U.S. access is OTC.
BELFB is a U.S.-listed small-cap underfollowed specialty-magnetics and power-products candidate; node exposure is plausible but requires revenue-materiality verification.

POWL should be tracked as an adjacent switchgear/power-distribution reference rather than a dry-type transformer pure play; it can help test whether transformer and switchgear bottlenecks are moving together.

HUBB has direct data-center power-quality, active harmonic filter, PDU transformer, and modular switchboard product evidence, but diversified-company dilution makes it better as a reference than an underfollowed alpha candidate.
Layer 2 should quantify revenue mix, backlog, lead times, and capacity expansion for HMDPF and BELFB; current Layer 1B evidence proves product adjacency but not yet earnings sensitivity.

HMDPF/HPS.A should remain a priority candidate for the dry-type-transformer and power-quality node because company disclosures directly match dry-type transformers, power-quality products, related magnetics, digital infrastructure, and backlog growth.

POWL is not a dry-type transformer pure-play but is a strong adjacent candidate for switchgear, e-houses, power-control rooms, bus duct, and engineered power-distribution bottlenecks; verify data-center and utility order mix.

AMSC adds a less obvious power-quality lane through STATCOMs, voltage control, harmonic filters, and reactive compensation; survival in later layers depends on confirming grid-product revenue/backlog share.
HUBB should be treated as a reference/competitive anchor for scaled electrical and utility infrastructure exposure, not as the primary underfollowed discovery candidate.

PPSI appeared in searches but should be handled as a speculative shadow candidate only: current evidence points more to mobile/critical power and distributed generation after sale of electrical infrastructure assets, not direct dry-type transformer exposure.

Hammond Power Solutions should be tracked as the cleanest underfollowed public-market mapping for dry-type transformers and power-quality products; US access appears via OTC HMDPF while primary liquidity is TSX:HPS.A.

AMSC should be tracked as a power-quality and reactive-compensation candidate rather than a conventional transformer supplier; key evidence is D-VAR, actiVAR, VVO, NEPSI, and Neeltran contribution to Grid segment revenue.

Bel Fuse is a lower-confidence specialty magnetics and power electronics candidate; survival in later layers depends on proving data-center, AI-networking, or high-power architecture demand rather than generic electronics exposure.

Powell Industries is an adjacent reference for custom switchgear and integrated medium-voltage power distribution; include for context but avoid treating it as a pure dry-type transformer or power-quality supplier.

Need a later pass for non-US primary listings and OTC/ADR names in power-quality reactors, harmonic filters, cast-resin transformers, HVDC reactors, and transformer component suppliers; initial evidence suggests this may reveal additional underfollowed assets.

HMDPF / Hammond Power Solutions should be prioritized for later-layer verification as the cleanest identified public-market mapping to dry-type transformers, cast-resin transformers, power-quality products and engineered magnetics; U.S. OTC liquidity/listing status should be flagged.

POWL / Powell Industries is an adjacent chokepoint candidate for medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems; direct evidence of a >$400M data-center order and $1.8B backlog makes it important but potentially less underfollowed after recent attention.

BELFB / Bel Fuse is a lower-attention specialty magnetics and power-solutions hypothesis; include only if later evidence confirms meaningful exposure to data-center, utility, industrial electrification, power-quality or electrical-OEM demand.
HUBB / Hubbell should remain in the reference lane for diversified electrical and utility-infrastructure benchmarking, not the primary alpha-discovery lane.

Layer 2 should verify backlog, lead times, capacity expansions, customer concentration, named data-center/utility approvals, and margin durability for transformer, power-quality, magnetics and switchgear candidates before any thesis upgrade.
